en: The Scripture on the Eight Great Dhāraṇī Kings of the Vidyādhara-piṭaka,
spoken by the Buddha. Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heavens, Imperially Appointed Court Dispersing Grandee, Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial,
and Dharma-Transmitting Master, the Subject Shi Hu, in accordance with the Imperial Decree.
At that time, for the sake of sentient beings in the final age,
the World-Honored One proclaimed the *Sūtra of the Eight Great Dhāraṇī Kings of the Vidyādhara-piṭaka*,
so as to cause all practitioners among the fourfold assembly of the future to [attain realization].
He brings benefit to all sentient beings, and even seeks after all *siddhis* until he attains accomplishment.
The Buddha said: "If there is a practitioner..."
One who practices these eight great dhāraṇīs must arouse a courageous mind that is firm and non-regressive;
first, one must purify the body and mind, ensuring they are both internally and externally immaculate.
One must continue until accomplishment is attained without interruption;
if there is even a brief interruption, accomplishment will not be obtained.
If one wishes to perform the recitation and practice:
Each time you perform the recitation, you must first chant:
"Namo to all Buddhas, Dharmas, and the Assembly of Noble Ones.
Having thus completed the taking of refuge in the Triple Gem, recite with a devout mind.
Then he spoke the dhāraṇī, saying:
*Nama ācivāci naciṭake caṭake caṭe urumade rurumade turuhe mire sarvārthavipranāśanam namaḥ sarvasamantabuddhānām siddhyantu mantrapadāḥ svāhā*. This is the dhāraṇī.
This was indeed proclaimed by the past immeasurable Perfectly Enlightened Ones, the World-Honored Bipeds.
If one wishes to practice for the sake of sentient beings,
performing rites of pacification, enrichment, and protection, [one should do so].
First, one must recite with thorough mastery;
once the preliminary practices are accomplished and great power has been attained,
one may then act for the sake of sentient beings.
This dhāraṇī rite may be performed during the mid-autumn season, for it possesses great power.
If one performs it at this time, the recitation will easily achieve success,
and one will be able to eliminate the eight great fears.
Furthermore, if sentient beings constantly maintain and recite it,
they will always receive protection and enjoy peace and happiness day and night;
all inauspiciousness will be entirely dispelled.
Their merit and virtue will increase, and they shall be free from all suffering and affliction.
Whether in a royal capital or encountering the turmoil of war,
those who wish to escape various perils and difficulties [should do so].
Having selected an auspicious morning at the hour of midday,
one should perform the recitation ritual and shall attain liberation.
This applies even to those who have been afflicted by various demonic possessions caused by devas, nāgas, ghosts, or spirits.
It can also bring about their release. By the power of recitation,
even a withered tree can be made to sprout flowers and fruit once again.
It even enables the practitioner to attain knowledge of past lives and recognize the events of immeasurable births.
Furthermore, he spoke this dhāraṇī:
*Pūjvare pūjvare svasti mahāsattvamahājvare te huke muke huke muke mahāśrīṇi rāmitaye śeṣe śatru mahājvare jvalate siddhaya saṃjñā-māraṇiṇa svāhā.* This dhāraṇī.
This was proclaimed by the youth Arthasiddhi;
one may perform the recitation ritual for ten months to bring benefit to all sentient beings.
One shall obtain immeasurable, pure karmic fruits. Furthermore, he spoke this dhāraṇī:
Sūnataye sūvedanā uṇatye nirlatye vajre dhamare camanañci vaci tathābharu naṭa vaṭa ne nataye ikacaṭra ṭiṭṭhisajina rākṣasi caṭṭini huṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. This dhāraṇī...
This was proclaimed by the Pratyekabuddhas.
During the winter season, one should seek a pure location and perform the rite of recitation;
it is capable of protecting all sentient beings.
Furthermore, the dhāraṇī is spoken as follows:
*tara jiru jiru ve ru ve raṭa ke he le me le te le śi le naṭi vaṭi kunaṭi ana-mate mana-mate ro re ka-saka-sika-sa-śira-ro-ra-ma-dha-u-maye ni-pasa-pase oṃ vibhava-te svāhā*. This is the dhāraṇī.
This was proclaimed by ten million arhats;
it can protect all sentient beings and cause them to be free from all fears.
This dharma should be recited during the spring season.
By practicing the rites for pacifying calamities and increasing prosperity, one will surely attain accomplishment.
If one acts according to the Dharma without error, one's spiritual practice will not regress;
one may even achieve invisibility such that no one can see them.
Furthermore, the heart-dhāraṇī is spoken as follows:
Oṃ antardhāya me vibhava svāhā. This heart-mantra [should be used] for the sake of whatever is sought.
Furthermore, by reciting the name nine hundred thousand times (*navalakṣa*), whatever one seeks will surely be fulfilled. When the number is complete,
one should prepare various kinds of incense and flowers and light lamps to make offerings to the Buddha,
Dharma, and Saṅgha, as well as to Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, Śrāvakas, and others.
If you are a mendicant, you should take your alms-bowl and travel north.
Upon reaching a village, you may go on alms-round in successive order, limiting yourself to seven houses;

you must not skip over them. After receiving what is offered by those seven houses, the merit shall extend to seven generations of your kin. Regarding the flowers to be offered, you may seek *karavīra* flowers.
And with the Dragon-Flower [Buddha] and others as the most supreme, he further spoke this dhāraṇī:
*Svāni svāni svanā mukhe ruṣame saṃkhe mahākape oṃ jile mile oṃ kai ti vine yugaṃ kṣāṇaya svāhā*. This dhāraṇī was proclaimed by a Stream-enterer (*srotāpanna*).
This rite may be recited during the summer season to seek accomplishment.

As for the place where the ritual is performed, one should seek a charnel ground, or the area between two rivers, or a bridge. If performing it for the protection of another, one should establish the site for the recitation there.
First, seek out a pure maiden to join the threads and string the beads together;
recite one hundred thousand (*lakṣa*) times to achieve the desired accomplishment.
Alternatively, take blood from the left rib of one's own body.
Perform the homa with white lotuses;
by reciting [the mantra] eight hundred times, all that is sought shall be attained.
Alternatively, one may use the left eye of a black cat, a dead pig, or a deceased person.
Grind these three ingredients together with mercury (rasa) into a single pill.
Take it along with the sap of the śāla tree;
whatever one seeks will certainly be accomplished.
Furthermore, the dhāraṇī is spoken as follows:

Akase akase nakase gaṇakare prajñāna-dam prajñāna-vatva oṃ vidha mahā-vidha-se na-peta na-petu ru-ru-mi-hi-jile-mile ajita jina-rāja-mi-tūya namo sarva-buddha-sambuddha-svabhāvānāṃ svāhā. This is the dhāraṇī.
This was proclaimed by the Bodhisattva Aparājita.
If one recites it with a sincere mind for one year,
one will certainly obtain superior physical strength, excellence, auspiciousness, and peace and happiness.
Endowed with merit, his fame spread far and wide.
He further spoke this dhāraṇī:
*Namo raudrāntakṣayāya | namo nāgemyaḥ | namo rākṣasībhyo | namo dānaviyogakāriṇyai | ye ānabhivijñapti ku ku umbudha khaga cakre svāhā.* This is the dhāraṇī.
This was proclaimed by the Anāgāmin;
it can save one from all suffering of illness.
If there is a patient, the practitioner should hold their hand and recite this.
Consecrate breast milk for them to drink and for them to bathe their bodies;
even if they are at the point of death, they may still be cured.
Alternatively, one may consecrate *maṇaśila* medicine with mantras.
If placed in the ears of a sick person, it will also bring about recovery.
If there is a practitioner who has completed their preliminary practices and wishes to seek *siddhi*,
they may hold either a rosary or a wheel.
If one merely recites according to the ritual,
even if the practitioner lacks merit,
they will still attain accomplishment through the power of the Dharma.
Furthermore, the dhāraṇī is spoken as follows:

*Vasani kāri vasani makari vasani makari vasani takari takari vasani makari vasani rūrari vasani vasanākari tinaṃo āzarīya paṇānāṃ oṃ vasani sulomi ke svāhā*. Regarding this dhāraṇī, when I was formerly a bodhisattva in the past...
Known as the Vidyārāja Subhamati,
he manifests his body among quadrupeds and speaks this dhāraṇī to bring about benefit.

If there are those who receive and uphold this with a sincere heart, their aspirations shall be fulfilled. If there are sentient beings who have committed various evil karmas and are destined to fall into the realm of animals, by the majestic power of this dhāraṇī, [they shall be liberated].
It eradicates prior transgressions and ensures certain rebirth among humans or devas.
This dhāraṇī can accomplish various types of undertakings.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who wishes to achieve success in various undertakings, [they should practice it].
One must first practice the preliminary rites until they are perfected;
only then should one employ the substances required for the desired accomplishment.
Before the Great Vidyārāja,
recite the mantra either three times or six times each day,
limiting the recitation to one thousand repetitions per session.
One must not allow any deficiency until *siddhi* is attained; once *siddhi* has been obtained, the task is fully accomplished.
If a person wishes to subjugate an enemy, they should sit facing south.
Draw the head and face of the enemy with one's hand and press it down while reciting the mantra; the enemy will naturally be subdued.
If a person constantly recites this three times each day, [the result will be achieved].
One will gain the reverence and submission of all people.
If one faces south and performs homa with black sesame seeds, whatever matters one seeks in one's heart will be attained one by one.
If one places the alms bowl on the ground and presses upon it while performing the empowerment, one will certainly obtain abundant offerings.
Furthermore, if one empowers clarified butter and consumes it,
one will never suffer from malaria and will always experience constant ease and tranquility.
Furthermore, if a woman has no milk,
by consecrating ghee and salt and having her eat them, she will have milk. Moreover,
if a woman has no children, [the same applies].
Consecrate sandalwood flowers by grinding them into powder;
apply them to the forehead three times each day.
Alternatively, bind the medicinal substance around the neck or the upper arm, and one will certainly give birth to a son endowed with merit.
Furthermore, if a woman is of a wicked nature,
her husband’s recitation of the empowerment (adhitiṣṭhanā) will immediately transform her disposition into one that is gentle and virtuous.
Likewise, if a husband is of a wicked nature...
The wife recited mantras over powdered sandalwood flowers and had him eat them;
immediately, they came to hold one another in deep esteem.
Furthermore, if a person crosses a river and reaches its middle, where the current is deep, [the mantra should be applied].
If his physical strength fails and he fears sinking,
by bringing it to mind, he immediately finds shallow water;
or he may empower a withered tree so that it again produces flowers and leaves.
If one performs empowerment over a dried-up pond, water will spontaneously fill it to the brim.
Furthermore, the dhāraṇī is spoken as follows:
*sādye akāci vikāci pūṇe āgate samahite siddhisamade svapnāṃ namo sta ācalyāna*. Regarding this dhāraṇī, in the past...
This was proclaimed by the Extremely Wrathful Vidyārāja.
If one constantly upholds it,
one shall obtain auspicious and supreme attainments.
If a person has completed the preliminary practices through recitation, they should take the powdered kernels of *piṇḍīra* flowers and *bimbi* fruits.
Afterwards, they should mix these with clarified butter and honey, ignite them,
and then consume them together with consecrated milk.
If one subsequently performs recitation for seven days and nights, one will attain great intelligence.
Furthermore, if one takes the eyes of a tiger, a wild fox, a cat, a pig,
or other such animals, and grinds them into powder;
Mix equal portions together to form pills;
by reciting mantras over them and placing them inside the nostrils, one shall attain invisibility.
Alternatively, if using the medicinal root of *mṛdvīkā* (grape-vine), [the same result is achieved].
Mix it with milk and honey;
by consuming it while empowered with mantras, one attains a countenance that does not age.
Whether in a cemetery, beneath a solitary tree, or at a crossroads, [one should perform this].
In such a place, one should perform the recitation while fasting;
if success is attained, one will be able to travel and dwell in the sky,
and may also roam through the realms of the desire and form heavens.
If one attains the accomplishment of the sword, it is the most supreme.
Whether at the seashore or the banks of a great river,
one should constantly consume milk or meat broth.
If one recites this for ten months,
maintaining daily practice with body and mind undeterred,
one will certainly obtain extraordinary treasures from the sea or from within rivers.
If one constantly eats mung beans and ghee while performing recitation at a place on a mountain where a nāga resides,
one will obtain pearls and gold sent by the nāga.
If one recites the mantra beneath an udumbara tree,
constantly begging for alms and reciting without interruption until the mantra is accomplished through clarified butter (ghṛta).
In a mere moment it becomes water;
by drinking it, one attains liberation from the various phenomena of the world.
If one fashions a lion out of clay and consecrates it with mantras...
If one attains accomplishment, one may ascend by means of it to the celestial realms.
Thus, if one seeks accomplishment, one should practice each of these dharmas individually.
Once the preliminary practices have been perfected, one must recite [the mantra] eight thousand times according to the ritual rules; one will certainly attain siddhi.
At that time, the World-Honored One, having spoken these eight great dhāraṇī-kings of the Vidyādharapiṭaka, [concluded].
He addressed Ānanda, saying:
"You must skillfully receive and uphold this secret dharma,
so that it may be transmitted without interruption into the future."
"May this bring great benefit to practitioners and to all sentient beings.
Then Ānanda, having received the Buddha’s instruction,
rejoiced with leaping joy, prostrated, and withdrew.
The Sūtra on the Eight Great Dhāraṇī Kings of the Vidyādharapiṭaka Spoken by the Buddha.
